title: Reading words that start with un and re
examples: What does re mean in redo?

explain.say: Some words have a little front door. Look at unhappy on the board. The front door is un. Read the door, then read the word you know behind it.

draw.text: Reading words that start with un and re

explain.say: Look at the front part glowing: un. It means not, so it flips the meaning of a word. Can you make a thumbs down and say un?
Now the word behind it: happy. You know that one! Un plus happy: unhappy means not happy. Can you show me an unhappy face, then a happy one?
Here is another front door: re. It means again. Re plus do: redo means do it again. If you make a mistake, you can always redo it. What do you think reread means?
Look at the two families on the board. Spot the front door, then read the word behind it. Wonderful! Challenge: what does refill mean?

faq.q: What does un mean at the start of a word?
faq.a: un usually means not. Unhappy means not happy, and unkind means not kind. Sometimes it means undo, like unlock.

faq.q: What does re mean at the start of a word?
faq.a: re usually means again. Redo means do again, and replay means play again.
A prefix is a small part at the front of a word that changes its meaning, like un and re.

faq.q: How do I read a word with a prefix?
faq.a: Cover the prefix with your finger and read the word you know. Then uncover the prefix and read the whole word.

faq.q: Does every word starting with re mean again?
faq.a: No. In words like red and read, the r and e are just part of the word. Check: is there a real word left after the re?

facts: A prefix is a group of letters added to the start of a word to change its meaning.
The prefix un often means not, and the prefix re often means again.

quiz.why: un means not, so unkind means not kind.

wrong.1: un does not mean very. It flips the meaning.
wrong.2: Again is the job of re, not un.

quiz.why: re means again, so replay means play again.

wrong.1: Not is the job of un, not re.
